title: Rule 90 inside Lenia

rule90_check.reference: integer XOR of left and right neighbours on the same ring

why_it_works: R = 2 poly kernel core is zero at r = 0 and r = 1, so on a 1-D ring it puts weight 1/2 on each nearest neighbour and none on the cell. U is 0, 1/2 or 1. With T = 1, A <- clip(A + G(U)) gives 1 when G(U) ~ +1 (U = 1/2, one neighbour on) and 0 when G(U) ~ -1 -- exactly Rule 90. exp growth leaves residues of order 2e^(-12.5) ~ 7e-6.
view: space-time diagrams: x = cell, y = step (downward); inferno, nearest-neighbour
caveats: Classic Lenia's radially symmetric kernel cannot express left-right asymmetric rules such as Rule 30 or Rule 110 exactly; see claim C061 for the set that the discrete limit reaches.
T = 1 (dt = 1) is far outside the usual Lenia regime (T = 10 for Orbium); this is the discrete limit Chan 2019 sec. 2.1.6 uses to embed Game of Life.
